Title: Sacrorum conciliorum nova, et amplissima collectio ... quae Joannes Dominicus Mansi evulgavit. Tomus Septimus: ab anno CCCCLI ad annum CCCCXCII inclusive
Creator: Giovanni Domenico Mansi (ed.), after Philippe Labbe, Gabriel Cossart and Nicolas Coleti
Publisher: Facsimile reproduction for H. Welter, Paris and Leipzig, of the Florence edition 'expensis Antonii Zatta Veneti'
Publication Date: 1901 (the facsimile: 'Editio iterata ad Editionis principis exemplum ab Huberto Welter ... Parisiis MDCCCCI' at file line 182; 'H. WELTER' at 106; the original edition is catalogued by archive.org as 1762)
Rights: Public Domain (pd-us-by-date: the 1901 facsimile date is printed at file line 182; the underlying edition is of the 18th century); the item record carries no rights field
Language: lat (Latin, with the Greek of the conciliar acts printed in parallel; the OCR renders the long s as f and recovers the Greek column only in part)
Source: archive.org item sacrorumconcilio0007joan (catalogue title 'SACRORUM CONCILIORUM', volume 7, catalogue date 1762, contributor Internet Archive), full text at https://archive.org/download/sacrorumconcilio0007joan/sacrorumconcilio0007joan_djvu.txt. Fetched directly 2026-10-17 by the Shared-Events source-research thread (Era 2 worker D); the byte count of the downloaded file (3,639,503) equals the size archive.org lists for the djvu.txt.
Provenance note: Extracted unaltered: the item's own djvu.txt is reproduced whole after this header; nothing was stripped, normalized or corrected. Rights basis: the 1901 facsimile date read in the OCR of the title page places the printing out of US copyright under this project's pd-us-by-date rule; the text reproduced is that of the 1762 edition, older still.
Content note: Mansi tomus 7, 451 to 492 (span at file line 159): the remaining sessions of Chalcedon from 'ACTIO QUINTA' (9189), with the Definition of Faith ('Sequentes igitur sanctos patres', 10861), the canons (238 in the index) including canon 28, the council's letters to Leo and Marcian, Leo's letters after the council, and the Codex Encyclius of 457-458 (index 396), the collected replies of the provincial synods to the emperor Leo on Chalcedon and on Timothy Aelurus. Latin and Greek primary documents of Chalcedon, sessions V onward, and of its first reception.
